core_obligations: Prorepresentable implies the conditions (proof lines 5747-5760): a prorepresentable functor is a deformation functor, its tangent space is finite dimensional, and the comparison map from the derivations of the residue field is identified with the corresponding map of derivations of R, which is injective because the quotient map R -> k is surjective.

Reduce the converse to the tangent spaces (proof lines 5762-5768): by the deformation functor axioms (S1) and (S2) hold, so the existence theorem provides a minimal versal formal object xi over R whose differential has bijective orbits on the derivations of the residue field.

Conclude the isomorphism (proof lines 5768-5772): the action of the derivations of the residue field on the source is free by hypothesis (c), and the differential is bijective on orbits, so it is bijective; by the minimality criterion for smooth morphisms of functors the transformation represented by xi is an isomorphism, which is prorepresentability of the functor.
proof_roadmap: Verify the three conditions for a prorepresentable functor.
In the converse use the axioms to obtain a minimal versal formal object.
Use freeness of the action and bijectivity on orbits to upgrade to an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The theorem proves that a functor on the category of Artinian algebras is prorepresentable exactly when it is a deformation functor, has finite dimensional tangent space and the comparison map from the derivations of the residue field into the tangent space is injective (statement lines 5738-5745). The proof (proof lines 5747-5775) verifies the three conditions for a prorepresentable functor, and in the converse produces a minimal versal formal object and upgrades it to an isomorphism using freeness of the action and bijectivity on orbits. H3: the converse combines two nontrivial theorems with an orbit argument, written out in full.
